correctness.rationale: The plane quartic is smooth because its gradient is (Z^3,X^3,Y^3). Exact Taylor expansion gives the hyperflex criterion P^(9)=[z:x:y], and solving it on the curve gives the separable degree-28 polynomial t^28+t^21+1. Its displayed factorization fixes bitangent Frobenius orbits, and the hyperflex tangent map is injective. In F_729, a standalone pure-Python verifier enumerates all 728 nonzero field elements and every one of the 378 bitangent pairs; 63 normalized intersections each occur six times and pass through exactly four lines, with Frobenius orbit counts 3 size-3 and 9 size-6. A finite computation is conclusive here only because the prior parametrization proves it is exhaustive. The final verifier is included and is executable with no outside data. The newly accepted content is the complete arithmetic incidence-point decomposition, not the recovered input bitangent polynomial.

originality.rationale: A prior exact result on this same F3 Klein model, item 8f153f4c-7a23-40b3-b68f-5e2b15b83765, already supplies the polynomial t^28+t^21+1, the 28 bitangents and their Frobenius cycles 1,3,6,6,6,6. Those are unequivocally prior and not part of the new originality claim. Elkies (1998/99) also covers Hermitian geometry and 28 hyperflexes, and generic unitary geometry supplies the 63 geometric concurrence points. The new result is the full 63-point arithmetic incidence-scheme splitting into three degree-three and nine degree-six closed points, including the exact all-n rational-point formula. An abstract 28-line cycle multiset does not determine which pairs become concurrent in each orbit, so the new 63-point Frobenius permutation is not implied by the earlier 28-line orbit data alone. Meagher–Top (2010) excludes characteristic 3 in their detailed Klein section, and characteristic-zero bitangent arrangement tables have different incidence; targeted mathematical literature and published-record searches produced no equivalent arithmetic concurrence classification. Residual possibility remains of an implicit computation in finite unitary geometry or a differently presented projective twist.
residual_risks: Exact 28-line polynomial and cycle types are explicitly covered by earlier own work and must not be claimed as new.
An unlocated unitary-geometry Galois-incidence table or projective twist calculation might already give the 63-point cycle type 3*3+9*6.

value.rationale: The 63 singular points of the full 28-bitangent arrangement are an intrinsic, natural zero-dimensional incidence scheme in the canonical plane embedding of a genus-three curve. The previous exact 28-line Frobenius cycles leave its Galois permutation undetermined because concurrence is extra geometric information about triples and quadruples of lines, not merely an orbit statistic. Classifying the full 63-point arithmetic scheme gives its minimal fields, excludes small-field singular intersections, and gives the exact rational-point count over every finite extension. This is a complete motivated arithmetic invariant of a distinguished classical incidence configuration rather than a routine increment of the previously known 28-line count. It also distinguishes the characteristic-three arithmetic twist from the standard F9-split Hermitian model.
